import json
import pandas as pd
from collections import defaultdict
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load chat JSON file
with open("chat.json", "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    chat_data = json.load(f)

# Count messages per 30-second bucket
buckets = defaultdict(int)
for comment in chat_data["comments"]:
    time = int(comment["content_offset_seconds"])
    bucket = (time // 30) * 30
    buckets[bucket] += 1

# Create a DataFrame
df = pd.DataFrame(sorted(buckets.items()), columns=["time_sec", "message_count"])

# Add rolling average and spike detection
df["rolling_avg"] = df["message_count"].rolling(window=5, min_periods=1).mean()
df["is_spike"] = df["message_count"] > df["rolling_avg"] * 1
df["timestamp"] = pd.to_timedelta(df["time_sec"], unit='s')

# Show spikes only
spikes = df[df["is_spike"]][["timestamp", "message_count", "rolling_avg"]]
print(spikes)

# Export spikes to CSV
spikes.to_csv("chat_spikes.csv", index=False)

# Optional: Visualize
plt.figure(figsize=(12,5))
plt.plot(df["timestamp"], df["message_count"], label="Message Count")
plt.plot(df["timestamp"], df["rolling_avg"], label="Rolling Avg", linestyle="--")
plt.scatter(spikes["timestamp"], spikes["message_count"], color='red', label="Spikes")
plt.title("Twitch Chat Activity Over Time")
plt.xlabel("Timestamp")
plt.ylabel("Messages per 30s")
plt.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("chat_spike_graph.png")
plt.show()
